title: Spanish Tortilla
subtitle: Thick potato and egg omelette, best served at room temperature
excerpt: A proper tortilla espanola takes patience with the potatoes and nerve at the flip. The result is a golden, creamy round of tender potato and soft egg that tastes just as good cold as it does warm. Simple ingredients, careful cooking.
sourceNotes: Based on traditional Spanish tortilla espanola technique. The slow-cooking potato method follows classic Basque and Castilian approaches.

content.text: Cook the potatoes slowly in the oil so they soften without browning. They should confit rather than fry. Browning the potatoes will make the finished tortilla dry and crumbly.

Heat the olive oil in a 28cm frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the potato and onion slices. Season with salt. Cook gently for 20 minutes, turning occasionally, until the potatoes are tender but not browned.
Beat the eggs well in a large bowl and season generously. Use a slotted spoon to lift the potato and onion out of the oil and straight into the eggs. Stir together and leave to sit for 5 minutes.

Pour most of the cooking oil out of the pan, leaving a thin coating. Heat the pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg and potato mixture. Shake the pan gently to settle it. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes until the base is set and the edges are firm.

Place a large flat plate over the pan. In one quick movement, flip the tortilla onto the plate. Slide it back into the pan uncooked-side down. Cook for another 3 to 4 minutes until just set in the middle. Slide onto a plate to serve.

items.fix: Run a spatula around the edge before flipping.
Remove from heat while the middle still looks slightly soft.

items.cause: Not cooked long enough in the oil.
items.fix: Cook them longer in the oil before adding to eggs.
